gloss: to set up; to start; to challenge

definitions.gloss: to set up; to lay (a trap)
definitions.explanation: To prepare a device, trap, or mechanism.

definitions.gloss: to start; to begin (something against someone)
definitions.explanation: To initiate an attack, challenge, or aggressive action.

definitions.gloss: to be in the middle of
definitions.explanation: Combined with other verbs to indicate an action has started but is incomplete.

examples.japanese: {森|もり}に{罠|わな}を{仕掛|しか}けた。
examples.english: I set a trap in the forest.

examples.japanese: {相手|あいて}チームが{攻撃|こうげき}を{仕掛|しか}けてきた。
examples.english: The opposing team launched an attack.

examples.japanese: {仕事|しごと}を{仕掛|しか}けたまま{帰|かえ}ってしまった。
examples.english: I went home leaving the work half-done.

notes:
{仕掛|しか}ける is a transitive verb ({他動詞|たどうし}) meaning to set something in motion or prepare something, often with strategic intent.

ASPECT (ている):
{仕掛|しか}けている indicates something is set up or an action has been initiated.

PARTICLE PATTERNS:
- [trap/device]を{仕掛|しか}ける — to set up [trap/device]
- [person]に[action]を{仕掛|しか}ける — to start [action] against [person]

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {罠|わな}を{仕掛|しか}ける (set a trap)
- {喧嘩|けんか}を{仕掛|しか}ける (pick a fight)
- {攻撃|こうげき}を{仕掛|しか}ける (launch an attack)
- {仕掛|しか}け (mechanism, gimmick)

COMPOUND FORM:
〜{仕掛|しか}ける/〜{仕掛|しか}け means "in the middle of doing" or "half-done":
- {読|よ}みかけの{本|ほん} (book one is in the middle of reading)
- {食|た}べかけ (half-eaten)

RELATED WORDS:
- {仕掛|しか}け: mechanism, trick, gimmick (noun)
- {仕掛|しか}け{花火|はなび}: fireworks display
